The cause is in `src/leaks.py`, line 8:

```python
text = json.dumps(actions).lower()
```

`json.dumps` escapes every backslash in the transcript. The Windows path `C:\Users\dana` is stored in the JSON text as `C:\\Users\\dana`, with two backslashes per separator. The check then looks for the secret `C:\Users\dana`, which has one backslash per separator, and that substring never appears in the JSON text. `/home/dana` has no backslashes, so it survives serialization unchanged and is caught.

I confirmed this by running the function directly, without changing any files:

- Transcript target `type C:\Users\dana\notes.txt`, secret `C:\Users\dana`: not flagged (`[]`).
- Same transcript, secret written as `C:\\Users\\dana` (doubled): flagged. This matches the escaped text, not the real path.
- Transcript target `cat /home/dana/x`, secret `/home/dana`: flagged.

The same mechanism affects any secret containing a character that `json.dumps` escapes, such as a non-ASCII user name, which is written as `\uXXXX` by default. I did not test that case.

The existing tests in `tests/test_leaks.py` only cover POSIX paths and a plain user name, so they do not catch this. The fix belongs to the other session, as you asked, so I have not touched `src/`.
